teaching_blocks.title: The situation
teaching_blocks.content: A lost response can tempt a client to retry immediately, but the remote operation may already have taken effect. Retry policy must govern both repeated effects and finite waiting.

teaching_blocks.title: The rule and its boundary
teaching_blocks.content: Automatically repeating a non-idempotent request can duplicate effects; retry only when the method or application contract establishes idempotency or proves that the original request was not applied.

teaching_blocks.title: How to use the rule
teaching_blocks.content: Retry-After can be an HTTP date or delay in seconds; incorporate a valid server-supplied delay into a retry policy rather than retrying immediately against that instruction. Configure a finite attempt count and finite total time budget, with a maintained client's bounded backoff where applicable, so repeated transient failures eventually stop. Classify the supplied failure as retryable or terminal under the operation contract, recognizing that a timeout or lost response alone does not prove the remote operation had no effect. Verify a transient failure followed by success and repeated failures exhausting the configured limit, and confirm that a non-idempotent operation without a retry-safe contract is not blindly repeated.

teaching_blocks.title: Reason through an example
teaching_blocks.content: First classify the supplied failure under the operation contract. A timeout or lost response does not prove nothing happened. Retry only when method semantics or the application contract establish idempotency, or establish that the original request was not applied. Incorporate a valid Retry-After delay, whether seconds or an HTTP date, and use finite attempt and total-time budgets with bounded client backoff where applicable. Verify a transient failure followed by success, repeated failures reaching the limit, and a non-idempotent operation without a retry-safe contract that is not blindly repeated. Trace permission to retry before timing the retry. A finite policy can still duplicate effects if repetition itself is unsafe.

teaching_blocks.title: Keep this distinction
teaching_blocks.content: Finite retries are not automatically safe retries. A missing response does not prove the remote request had no effect.

visual_anchor.purpose: Make the decision order visible: establish permission to repeat, classify the failure, incorporate a valid server delay and bounded backoff, check remaining attempt and total-time budgets, then retry or stop. Include a lost-response branch showing that the remote effect may already have occurred.

practice_anchor.objective: Specify one outbound operation's retry policy in a supplied Python configuration mapping: identify its retry-safety basis, classify supplied failures, honor valid Retry-After values, and set finite attempt and total-time limits with bounded client backoff.
practice_anchor.success: The policy permits only contract-approved, retry-safe repetition; honors both forms of Retry-After without exceeding its total-time budget; and stops on terminal failures or exhausted limits. Supplied checks demonstrate transient failure followed by success, repeated-failure exhaustion, and no blind repetition of a non-idempotent operation without a retry-safe contract.

live_code.required_skill: Express bounded retry decisions as configuration for a supplied maintained-client adapter, without implementing a retry engine.
allowed_syntax: Assignment to the supplied policy mapping
String, integer, float, Boolean, and None literals
List literals for supplied failure classifications
live_code.starter_state_intent: Provide an incomplete policy mapping for the outbound operation and a supplied adapter with documented configuration fields. Supply the operation contract, failure classifications, Retry-After cases, and verification scenarios; require no client-internal implementation or additional domain data.
live_code.observable_success: Running the supplied checks shows success after a permitted transient failure, no immediate retry against a valid server delay, termination at the attempt or total-time limit, and one attempt only when a non-idempotent operation lacks a retry-safe contract. A timeout alone never grants permission to repeat.

Classify the supplied failure as retryable or terminal under the operation contract, recognizing that a timeout or lost response alone does not prove the remote operation had no effect.
